$comment: Read from Google's own discovery document, not docs prose: presentations.create -> POST v1/presentations, request Presentation, response Presentation. The method creates a BLANK presentation and ignores request content; title is the only field this simple action sends.
title: Google Slides presentation
description: Create a blank Google Slides presentation.
$idempotencyComment: Google offers no idempotency key on presentations.create -- the discovery method declares no parameters and no idempotency header. So this is honestly unsafe-to-replay with no way to make it safe: a retried durable run creates a SECOND presentation.

config.label: Title
config.description: The title of the new blank presentation.
config.$comment: Presentation is a large response schema, but create is not a way to seed slides or layouts. Google's method says request content is ignored, so exposing those fields would accept configuration that can never work.

$presentationIdComment: The method can accept a caller-supplied presentationId and otherwise generates one. This action deliberately leaves ID generation to Google: exposing a client-chosen global resource id adds collision and validation concerns to an action whose purpose is simply to create a blank presentation by title.

outputShape.description: The id of the created presentation.

$outputComment: The Presentation is returned at the HTTP response top level. The connector runtime places that body under `data`; there is no provider-specific wrapper such as `{presentation: ...}`.

contract.$comment: The exact Presentation properties this action sends and reads. Drift-check projects these names from the discovery schema instead of treating the endpoint as unresearched.
